title: Balanced and unbalanced forces

match.reason: The closest bank point covers balanced and unbalanced forces well, but the new point also teaches that more mass needs a bigger force, which the bank card does not cover and which sits on a separate bank point, so it is broader than the match.

draft.title: Balanced and unbalanced forces
card: Forces are balanced when they are equal in size and opposite in direction, so they cancel out. The object stays still or keeps moving at a steady speed in a straight line.
Forces are unbalanced when one is bigger than the other. The overall force is not zero, so the object speeds up, slows down or changes direction.
A moving object does not need an unbalanced force to keep moving. It only needs one to change how it moves.
The more mass an object has, the bigger the unbalanced force needed to change its motion by the same amount.
draft.remember: Balanced forces mean no change in motion. An unbalanced force changes it.

a.q: A cyclist rides along a flat, straight path at a steady speed. What does this tell you about the forces on the bike?
opts: There are no forces on the bike
a.why: A steady speed in a straight line means there is no change in motion, so the forces are balanced. It is tempting to think a moving bike needs a bigger forward force, but that would make it speed up.

b.q: Two students push identical-looking trolleys with the same force. Trolley X is empty and trolley Y is full of books. Which result is most likely?
opts: X speeds up more than Y
Y speeds up more than X
X and Y speed up by the same amount
b.why: The same unbalanced force acts on both, but Y has more mass. The more mass an object has, the bigger the force needed to change its motion, so the empty trolley X speeds up more. Both trolleys speed up, because the push is an unbalanced force.
b.clue: Which trolley has more mass to get moving?

b.best: X speeds up more than Y
